document.title: Gangsta — development status board
document.purpose: A read-only description of how Gangsta is built, what it does, and what is planned. Written for another AI assistant to read before suggesting changes, so that advice fits the system instead of contradicting it.
howToUseThis: Read `constraints` first. Those are decisions already made and paid for. A suggestion that breaks one of them is wrong here even if it is good advice in general, and the `because` line says what it cost to learn.
`architecture` says which machine owns what. Most bad suggestions come from assuming one machine can write something another one owns.
`knownIssues` is honest, not marketing. If something is broken or unverified it is listed.
`notCovered` says what nobody has audited. Treat those areas as unknown rather than working.
document.maintainedBy: The coding assistant that works on the repository, in the same commit as the change it describes. Nothing on this board is generated from the owner's data, his notes or the commit history — it is written by hand so that it cannot leak anything personal.

overview.whatItIs: A single-user productivity and self-discipline companion. One person's own desktop app, their own phone, and a small always-on cloud process that stands in for the desktop while it is asleep.
overview.shape: Three programs sharing one state, with a strict rule about who may write what.
overview.notAProduct: There are no other users, no accounts and no multi-tenancy. Anything that assumes a user table, sign-up, or per-tenant isolation does not apply.

machines.name: PC
machines.stack: Electron 32 shell + Vue 3 / TypeScript front end + a Go backend process
machines.role: The authority. It owns every file of state and is the only machine that writes the canonical copy.
machines.detail: The Go process listens on 127.0.0.1 only. The renderer talks to it over a local HTTP RPC surface of about 442 methods. Nothing from the internet can reach it.

machines.name: Satellite
machines.stack: The SAME Go binary, built from the same source, running on Railway with satelliteMode = true
machines.role: Answers the phone while the desktop is closed, which is most of the day.
machines.detail: It holds a synced copy of the state and may change it, but its copy is not the truth: the PC overwrites it. Every change it makes is also queued as an operation for the PC to replay.

machines.name: Phone
machines.stack: Native Android (Java), package name MainFrame, in a separate repository
machines.role: A full client, not a viewer. It can create and change things offline.
machines.detail: It talks only to the satellite, over one base URL, every route under /phone/v1 (about 51 of them), authenticated with one shared credential sent as a header.

howStateMoves.ownership: The PC owns the files. The satellite owns nothing permanently.
howStateMoves.pcToSatellite: The PC pushes changed files by hash difference. A full push at most every 5 minutes; the relay folders every heartbeat.
howStateMoves.satelliteToPc: The satellite never gets to keep a change. It applies it to its own copy so the phone sees it at once, and queues an operation describing it. The PC pulls those operations and replays them through the same functions the desktop uses, then pushes the result back over the satellite's copy.
howStateMoves.whyThisOrder: On every tick the PC folds queued operations BEFORE it pushes state. That is what makes the satellite's optimistic write safe: the PC's version of the same change is always in place before its push overwrites what the satellite wrote.

storage.format: Plain JSON files in the OS application-data directory. No database, no ORM, no migrations framework.
storage.notSynced: Settings, which hold credentials, are never sent over the sync channel. Practice media is kept local on purpose.

dependencies.goThirdParty: None. The Go backend has an empty require block and uses only the standard library.
dependencies.whyItMatters: Suggesting a Go library is a bigger change than it looks. It would be the first one.

size.note: Line counts, not a quality claim.

constraints.rule: The PC owns the files. The satellite may apply a change locally, but must also queue an operation for the PC to replay.
constraints.because: The PC overwrites the satellite's copy whenever the two differ. A change written only on the satellite is reverted within five minutes, silently.

constraints.rule: Any operation that CREATES something needs an exactly-once ledger keyed by an operation id.
constraints.because: A batch of operations is re-delivered whole when an acknowledgement does not land. Idempotent operations survive that; a create makes a second thing. This has been fixed four separate times after the fact.

constraints.rule: Never mint an id from the clock.
constraints.because: The desktop runs on Windows, whose timer ticks about every 15ms. time.Now().UnixNano() returns the same value for consecutive calls — measured, it collided on the SECOND call, roughly 3000 duplicates in 3000 tries. Three id generators had this bug. Use crypto/rand.

constraints.rule: Tasks, daily notes and journal entries live in the JSON store, not in files on disk. Most of them have no file at all.
constraints.because: The app used to mirror them into a notes vault and no longer does. Any code that opens a task's file to find out what it says works for old records and fails for new ones — which looks random. This has been fixed five separate times.

constraints.rule: Decide retry-or-discard from the HTTP status code, never from the text of an error message.
constraints.because: The phone's outboxes used to search the error prose for '404'. A 404 is rendered as a sentence with no digits in it, so the one status it most needed to settle was the one it could never see, and the queue jammed behind it permanently.

constraints.rule: Drag and drop uses pointer events. Never the HTML5 drag-and-drop API.
constraints.because: Whether a drag begins is the platform's decision there. When it decides against, there is no event, no error and nothing the page can do — the cursor just flickers and nothing moves.

constraints.rule: The front end has no global box-sizing: border-box.
constraints.because: max-width caps the content box and padding adds on top of it. Layouts that assume the usual reset come out wider than expected.

constraints.rule: An assistant reply that claims an action happened must be true.
constraints.because: This app is a commitment device. Saying a block was lifted, a task saved or a change synced when it was not is the failure that makes the whole thing untrustworthy. Several past bugs were exactly this shape: the call reported success and did nothing.

constraints.rule: Deleting something permanently and taking it off a list are different acts and must not share a control.
constraints.because: Removing a shopping item from this trip keeps the item. Removing a target from a standing rule keeps the rule. A single 'remove' that guesses wrong has already destroyed a rule covering five other sites.

constraints.rule: The phone is a client that works offline. Every change goes through an outbox, is written to disk before anything is drawn, and is replayed in order.
constraints.because: It is used in places with one bar of signal. A design that needs a round trip to show a change is wrong for this app.

constraints.rule: Tests must be sabotaged before they are trusted.
constraints.because: Several tests here passed against the bug they claimed to cover. One matched any error containing 'not', which also matches 'cannot'.

constraints.rule: Finishing a learning resource pays no work points until the owner decides how it cannot be farmed.
constraints.because: Marking a video or link done is one click, and a click that mints points is exactly what the economy is built to refuse. The owner asked for the reward to stay undecided rather than guessed.

constraints.rule: A commitment or rule is broken only when the owner says so. Nothing reads activity, focus time, block rules or the warden to decide it.
constraints.because: The owner asked for this explicitly: there can be a good reason to break a promise, and only the owner knows it. A fine written by a machine is not a fine anyone agreed to.

implemented: Chat with an assistant persona that can call tools: scheduling, blocking, memory, tasks, quests
Calendar with a day, week and planning view; tasks and time blocks share one grid
Day planner that proposes what could fit in each stretch of a day, from a list of activities, open tasks and quests
Tasks and deadlines with quick-entry commands, priorities, recurrence, parking and archive
Skill tree with weekly quests, a work-point economy, per-skill coach chats, and a path for each skill that is discovered one step at a time
Self-imposed website and phone-app blocking with standing rules, schedules and negotiated passes
Shopping cart with user-defined columns, computed formulas, type lines and reference lists
Habit and daily tracking, journal, long-term and episodic memory
Activity tracking across desktop and phone, unified into one timeline
Alarm with a spoken wake-up pre-loaded to the phone so it rings with the desktop off
Workouts, recipes, practice boards, a pomodoro timer and an on-screen companion avatar

Commitments and rules: promises with a deadline and a fine in shekels, and standing rules with a fine per break. A timeline asks 'did you keep it?' when a deadline comes; a break can carry a good reason and then costs nothing; templates make a repeat commitment in one step. Moved in once from an outside database, which is left as it was.

On a phone-size screen the Crew board shows the skill tree the way the phone app draws it (the whole tree as branch panels, a branch as a focus tree or tiers, quests, campaign and a skill's window with its climb), with a switch to the PC view. The same read and write rules apply as in the PC view.
phoneCanDoAlone: Read and change the whole shopping cart
Plan a day, place and move blocks, confirm the day
Create and edit tasks and quests
Log workouts and recipes, tick habits, write journal entries
Hold a full assistant conversation, including per-skill coaching
Add, tick and pin learning resources on a skill, including by sharing a link from another app
Walk a skill's path: finish, split or block a step, plan the next one or ask for ideas, tie quests to steps, and keep what is known with its older versions
Answer commitments, report rule breaks, mark fines paid, and make commitments from templates

knownIssues.issue: The phone build with the Library is installed only when the phone is connected to the PC.
knownIssues.impact: Until it is, the phone has no Library tab and shows no routine or reward cards in chat. Nothing is lost; the next install switches it over.
knownIssues.status: waiting for the phone to be connected

knownIssues.issue: A read-back guard in the calendar's store-only write path is not covered by any test.
knownIssues.impact: It is defence against a store that writes and then cannot read back. Nothing can reach it while the store's own refusal stands, so it is unverified rather than known-good.

knownIssues.issue: Nothing records how long an individual task took, except when the user answers the "how long did that take?" buttons on a completion.
knownIssues.impact: Calibration's estimate-vs-actual stat now has one source instead of two. The old second source read each task's own file, which no longer exists, and the import that moved tasks into the store flattened their nested time entries down to the last session, so it could not be re-pointed without changing what the number means.

notCovered.note: Areas no review pass has examined. Treat them as unknown rather than working.
areas: The Vue front end outside the planner and calendar - there is a test runner for it now (`npm test`), but only the calendar header and the day-turn are covered
The alarm and its spoken missions
Concurrency across the package-level mutexes in the Go backend

inDevelopment.detail: A public, read-only description of the system, served by the always-on process and updated in the same commit as each change.

roadmap.item: Review the areas listed in notCovered
roadmap.why: Two review passes have found real bugs in every class they examined. The unexamined areas are not evidence of health.

roadmap.item: A live channel from the always-on process to the desktop
roadmap.why: Today the desktop polls every 20 seconds, so an action the cloud cannot perform itself waits that long. A held-open connection would make it immediate. Not started, and not urgent.

goodSuggestions: Changes that keep one machine as the owner of each piece of state
Changes that fail loudly rather than quietly
Changes that can be tested, and whose tests fail when the change is reverted
suggestionsThatWillNotFit: Adding a database, an ORM or a migrations framework — the state is plain JSON files on purpose
Adding a Go dependency — there are currently none
Multi-user features, accounts, sign-up or sharing — there is one user and no server-side identity
Anything that asks the cloud process to be the permanent owner of state
Anything that makes the phone depend on a round trip to show a change
Replacing the local RPC with a public API — the desktop backend binds to loopback deliberately
Detecting broken commitments or rules automatically from tracked activity or focus time — the owner decided against it

latestUpdates.item: Prompts: one voice, one order of priority, and history that remembers what happened
latestUpdates.detail: Every reply style used to end with 'short, funny, a bit sarcastic', placed right before his message where it outweighed the persona's own 'most replies have no joke'; tone now comes from the persona and the delivery rules only. 'Too detailed' no longer switches on long answers, and 'elaborate', 'in depth' and Hebrew asks do. The prompt now says which section wins when they disagree (honesty first). The model is told whether he writes from the phone or the desktop, and the desktop-only Freedom card is only described on the desktop. A past reply in the history now carries what it did (a grant, a card and whether it was accepted) and its mood tag, so the next turn knows and long chats keep their mood. Standing-rule notes in tool results are plain facts instead of capital-letter orders, so warden replies stop sounding like one template. The banter rule keeps the jokes, but now checks in once, as a friend, when something might be real.

latestUpdates.item: Out of credit is not 'slow down', slow is not offline, and the chat prefix caches
latestUpdates.detail: An empty prepaid balance comes back as the same status as a rate limit, so every call retried it four times and the background jobs kept calling; now it is recognised, never retried, pauses OpenAI calls for 15 minutes and says how to fix it. Offline now means a connection that could not be made: every HTTP client error used to count, so a long model call that hit its time limit switched the app to 'No internet'. The small-feature call path also checks offline and the pause before calling. The stable part of every chat request (persona, rules, tools, about 11,000 words of prompt) now carries an explicit cache marker on the gpt-6 models too, and all chats share one cache key, so a new chat no longer starts cold; if a model ever refuses the marker, the request is sent again without it and markers stay off for that run. The cache figure on the cost page now counts the misses (it averaged only the hits). Web search uses the current tool name.

latestUpdates.item: The chat's tools tell him what is really there
latestUpdates.detail: get_tasks now lists his open tasks, deadlines still ahead (soonest first) and what was done in the last week; it used to show only in-progress and MIT tasks plus five deadlines that could all be finished, so with 45 open tasks it showed 3. get_calendar shows the day's time blocks (work, sleep), so a working day no longer reads as empty and nothing gets booked inside a shift. Scheduling by title skips finished tasks and asks when two open tasks share a name. The three databases that moved out of the old notes service (productive list, commitments, recipes) are no longer offered to the chat while Gangsta's own store holds them, a new read-only get_recipes reads the recipe book, a text search there reads up to 500 rows instead of the first 25, and its answer is trimmed by whole rows instead of being cut mid-way. The recommender no longer treats rows from every connected database as things to do. A block rule cannot wait for a habit he does not have (the spelling is matched to his), and bad times or days are refused. get_day takes weekday names and says when a date is wrong; get_work_hours refuses a bad month instead of silently using this one. A retried turn no longer repeats a write whose arguments came back in another order, and every kind of refusal now shows as failed under the reply.

latestUpdates.item: Memory entries can be edited, moved and deleted on the Memory page
latestUpdates.detail: The Memory page could only add memories, so a wrong or outdated one could only be fixed by asking in chat. Each entry now has Edit, Move to another type, and Delete (with a confirm), and removals are kept in the local log. The page no longer calls memory append-only, and the empty legacy tab is hidden.

latestUpdates.item: Persona files can be rewritten through one guarded action
latestUpdates.detail: A single action now rewrites the persona files (personality, about-me, active state) or the old legacy memory file, and refuses every other path, and an empty personality. It exists for cleanups and a future editor: the persona files had no way to be corrected except by hand.

latestUpdates.item: Saved memories are found by meaning and ride along by themselves
latestUpdates.detail: The chat only reached memories outside the always-loaded core when the model chose to fetch them, and it chose to in none of the sixteen recorded turns. Every saved entry now has a short meaning vector (text-embedding-3-small, 256 numbers, kept beside the memory and synced, so the always-on process can search too). Each message is compared with them, and up to six clearly related entries (core types left out, about 1,600 characters at most) are added to that turn's tail; coach and thought chats get them as well, so a coach knows what he already told the main chat. Reconcile ranks related entries by meaning too. The vectors refresh a few seconds after any memory change; one message costs a tiny fraction of a cent. Entries can now be edited, moved to another type, or deleted one at a time, and removals are kept in the local log.

latestUpdates.item: Every chat feeds memory, and memory saves stop losing updates
latestUpdates.detail: Memory was only learned on the desktop chat page, so phone chats, coach chats and thought chats never fed memory while the prompt said memory saves itself. The backend now learns from every finished turn, including phone turns when the desktop folds them in (once per answer). Only exact copies count as duplicates now, so an update is no longer refused as 'already remembered'. A new entry is reconciled against related entries of every memory type, so an outdated copy filed elsewhere is replaced too; a save that removes something always adds the new entry, and every removed entry is kept in a local log. correct_memory changes one entry unless told otherwise and says when a memory type does not exist. Assistant rules are taken only from what the owner said himself. The chat's Save to Memory button files into a chosen memory type instead of a file the chat never read, feed answers go through the same save, memory writes are serialized, tags are built from the newest entries, a tag fetch returns every type that has it, an empty weekly rollup is no longer saved, the alarm reads his profile and goals first, and the memory switch also turns off the memory tools, the Brain and the feed.

latestUpdates.item: The always-on process follows his own settings, kill switch first
latestUpdates.detail: His settings file never leaves the desktop because it holds his keys, so the always-on process answered every phone chat on built-in defaults: it kept the warden on even when he had switched it off on the desktop, and it used default reply style, web search and model choices. The desktop now writes a separate copy of only the safe fields (the warden switch and curfew hours, reply style, web search, model choices, memory switches) whenever settings are saved and at startup, and it syncs like any other file. The always-on process lays it over its defaults on every read; with no copy yet it keeps the old default.

latestUpdates.item: Blocks tell the truth, come back on time, and only hold what he flagged
latestUpdates.detail: A timed phone pass ('unblock it for 10 minutes') now really comes back: before, it deleted a normal block for good while the tool said it would re-arm. Re-arms of warden grants and phone passes are now kept in a file, so a restart inside the window no longer loses them, and the Settings kill switch empties that file, so nothing comes back after the warden is switched off. delete_block_rule now fails for an id that does not exist instead of saying 'Rule deleted', says what the rule held, and logs it. On the satellite, a timed pass is timed, 'for good' and 'remove' are done by the PC on its next sync, and every queued warden decision carries an op id so it runs once. Refusals from the calendar and memory tools start with 'error', so the satellite no longer reports them as done. The watcher, the night curfew and the app-hop counter now hold only what the owner flagged himself (his Activity categories, or what he told Gangsta in chat); the warden's own verdicts become suggestions in its ledger and can never overwrite his. Every phone block records who set it, the warden lets go only of its own, and the status tool says who holds each block instead of calling them all the warden's. 'remove' is used only when he asks for a block to end.

latestUpdates.item: Every decision in a chat is made by the strong model; OpenAI keeps nothing
latestUpdates.detail: A chat turn's cheap reading rounds used to keep every tool, so the cheap model, whose prompt had none of the warden rules, memory or persona, made the access decisions: all six grant or refuse calls in the trace were made there. Now rounds 1 and 2 always run on the strong model with the full rules and every tool. Cheap rounds may only start after that, may only read, and hand the turn back to the strong model, which makes any change and writes the reply. The last answer round keeps the same tool list with tool_choice none, so it reads from the cache instead of starting a new prefix. /task and /quest force their tool with tool_choice instead of words. The warden's forced round now needs the message to name something that is blocked (or the turn to have looked at the blocks), keeps the tool list, and replaces the first reply only when it really decided. Every request sends store:false, so OpenAI no longer keeps a 30-day copy of every reply.

latestUpdates.item: The freeze check no longer waits behind page calls
latestUpdates.detail: The check that restarts Chromium's frozen network helper now asks the backend by 'localhost' instead of 127.0.0.1. The window keeps at most six connections per address and the backend answers one call at a time, so during a long chat turn the pages' own calls could fill all six and make the check think the network froze. The pages' change poll also waits for its answer before asking again, instead of stacking a new call every four seconds.

latestUpdates.item: Pages stay loaded after the PC sleeps
latestUpdates.detail: After a night of sleep every page in the desktop app stayed empty, while the local backend answered every call in milliseconds. The cause was Chromium's network helper process: alive, idle, and never returning an answer to the app. The desktop app now checks every 30 seconds, and soon after each wake-up, by asking the backend both through Chromium and through Node's own fetch. When Node gets an answer and Chromium does not, twice in a row, it restarts the network helper and reloads the windows. It never acts when the backend itself is down, and never twice within a minute.

latestUpdates.item: The shopping cart fits a small window
latestUpdates.detail: In a narrow window the saved lists squeezed the To buy receipt until the item names had no room at all and the prices were cut off. The saved lists now move under the receipt when there is not room for both, and on a narrow receipt (or + Add ticket) the company sits under the name instead of in its own column. Checked in a browser at 1150, 900 and 800 pixels wide.

latestUpdates.item: One spelling per category and company; left-to-right cart; Library pictures reach the phone
latestUpdates.detail: A category or company typed with other capitals or spaces now takes the spelling the cart already uses, so 'groceries' joins 'Groceries' instead of becoming a second chip. The shopping cart shows every name left to right, Hebrew too, on the PC and the phone, so its columns line up. And a routine step picture changed on the PC now reaches the phone: the PC never wrote down the phone changes it had applied, so the satellite kept serving its own frozen copy of the Library. It writes them down now, and the satellite also stands down once the PC has taken every change and sent a newer file. The satellite stands down once no phone change is still waiting, the last one is at least ten seconds old, and the PC's file arrived after it; and the PC now sends the Library right after taking phone changes, before it confirms them.

latestUpdates.item: The shopping cart, redesigned on the phone
latestUpdates.detail: The phone's To buy is the same dark receipt as the PC, with torn edges: the company in bold under each name, line prices, a total, and ticked items at the bottom under 'in the basket'. A type is a normal row; a tap opens its products in a drop-down. '+ Add' opens a centred ticket listing what the tab and the filters allow, adds one per tap and stays open; 'Create' opens the full editor with the same category rules as the PC, and 'New type' makes a type at the shelf. The editor is a ticket with company, categories and type picked from the existing ones. Groceries and All have striped rows.

latestUpdates.item: The shopping cart, redesigned on the PC
latestUpdates.detail: The To buy tab is now a dark receipt: items and types in one list, the company in bold on every line, the price of each line and a total at the end. Ticked items move to the bottom under 'in the basket'. A type is a normal row that says 'choose'; pressing it opens its products in a drop-down that floats over the list. The saved lists sit in a narrow column beside it. '+ Item' became '+ Add': a centred ticket with every item the tab and the filters allow, already-on-the-list ones marked with how many; a press adds one and it stays open. A new item always opens the full editor, with Groceries filled in on the Groceries tab, or the filter when exactly one is on. The item editor, 'Add a list to the cart' and the type picker became tickets too. Groceries and All stay a table, now with striped rows.

latestUpdates.item: A PC app's category sticks, and the Activity columns line up
latestUpdates.detail: Changing the category of some PC apps on Activity seemed to do nothing: the choice was saved under the program's name in small letters, and the app is reported with capital letters, so the rule was never found. A rule now matches its app however it is spelled, with or without capitals or .exe, and saving a new choice replaces the app's older rule under another spelling. On the Activity rows the device tag, the category and the time now have fixed widths, so they line up down the list.

latestUpdates.item: Striped rows in the lists
latestUpdates.detail: Every second row is now a little lighter, so long lists are easier to follow: Tasks, Commitments (the timeline, templates, rules and breaks), Activity, What Now (Watch Later and the Productive list), and the Back End's call list and database tables. Each group starts again with the normal color. A row with its own color, such as a selected or done task or the row under the mouse, keeps it. PC only.

latestUpdates.item: A new Library picture shows at once, and the object is the subject
latestUpdates.detail: Generating a picture again for a step made a new picture, but the page kept showing the old one, because the new file had the same name. Every new picture now gets a new name, and the old file is removed. The default style also changed: the step's object (a glass of water, a pill, a pair of shoes) is the main subject, shown like an old advertisement's product shot. A man is drawn only for a step no object can show, like walking or stretching.

latestUpdates.item: Library pictures in the recipe book's vintage style
latestUpdates.detail: Generate a picture on a Library step now paints in the same 1950s advertising style as the recipe book, rewritten for steps: an action shows a man doing it, and an item or an amount shows that item. The picture stays square, to fit the prints. The style text is in Settings, on a new Library page, and can be changed there like the recipe style; saving it empty puts the default back.

latestUpdates.item: The Library on the phone, and its chat cards
latestUpdates.detail: The phone has the Library too: the routines in a row of round icons at the top, and the routine on show as a board of prints, two to a row. A tap marks a step done for today and shows at once; a long press opens the step's menu, with a photo from the phone's gallery or a painted picture first, then mark done, edit, move and delete. The gear has 'Generate images for done steps', start over, rename and delete. A photo or a painted picture is made on the PC, because pictures live in a synced folder; the phone says so and the picture shows once the PC has synced. The routine and reward cards Gangsta drafts in chat now show on the phone with the same Add button. On the satellite, Add puts the item in at once and queues the same Accept for the PC; both ends take the item's id from the card, so nothing is added twice.

latestUpdates.item: The Library: routines as a board of photo prints (PC)
latestUpdates.detail: A new Library page holds the user's routines, such as waking up, each one a set of steps in order (put on pants, drink 1500 ml of water). Each step is a photo print pinned to a board, with its amount under it. Clicking a print marks the step done for today: the picture turns grey under a large green DONE stamp, and the next step says 'You are here'. Ticks are kept for today only and clear the next day; there is no history, by choice. A right-click on a step adds the user's own photo, paints one with the image model (paid), removes the picture, or edits, moves or deletes the step; until a step has a picture it shows an emoji. The gear holds 'Generate images for done steps', start over, rename and delete. In chat, Gangsta can draft a routine on a card, and the card's Add button puts it in the Library. Adding a shop reward from chat now works the same way: Gangsta prices it on a card and the Add button puts it in at that price, in place of saying yes.

latestUpdates.item: Watch: the buttons above a tall video fit again
latestUpdates.detail: On a tall, phone-shaped video, the buttons above the player ran off its right edge and the close button was cut off. They now wrap onto a second line under the title when there is no room.

latestUpdates.item: Practice clips zoom, and open in a window of their own
latestUpdates.detail: A clip on a practice board can now be zoomed: the mouse wheel zooms in where the mouse is, a drag moves the picture, and a double-click puts it back. The clips have a small player of their own for this, because the built-in video controls grew with the picture and slid away. Each clip can also open in its own window, which can go on another screen at any size; it has a keys menu that opens and closes, and a key tapped there plays both clips from their own marks. While a clip is out, the board shows where it is, and its keys, marking and both-play buttons work with the window. Closing the window puts the clip back on the board where it stopped. This is on the PC only.

latestUpdates.item: Gangsta adds and removes shop rewards in chat
latestUpdates.detail: The user can now ask Gangsta in chat to put a reward in the shop. Gangsta prices it with the same step as the shop's own button, tells the user the price, the wait and why, and adds it only after the user says yes in a later message; the code refuses an add in the same answer that proposed it. The reward goes in at the price the user was shown. Gangsta can also take a reward out of the shop when asked. This works in phone chat too, through the satellite. Fixed the same day: when the user said yes, Gangsta looked the price up again before adding it, and that look-up marked the price as not yet answered, so the add was refused. Looking it up again now keeps the price the user was shown, and a plain yes in chat is enough.

latestUpdates.item: Shop time opens the night curfew too
latestUpdates.detail: Time bought in the shop only opened the user's block rules, so an app held by Gangsta's night curfew stayed shut and the shop still said it was open. A pass now opens Gangsta's own blocks as well: the curfew and the warden's blocks, on the PC browser, the phone browser and the phone's apps. The pass is read each time a block list is served, so nothing is lifted and put back by a timer: when the time ends or the buy is undone, the block is there on the next read. The shop now lists what the curfew and the warden hold, and names what is blocking each app. A list block the user started by hand is not for sale; the shop says so and takes no WP.

latestUpdates.item: The shop: rewards Gangsta prices, and time on blocked apps
latestUpdates.detail: WP is now spent in a shop on the PC and the phone. A reward is something real the user writes down; Gangsta's model says how many days of saving it is worth (1 to 60) and how long to wait between two buys, with one reason, and the shop turns the days into WP: 6 WP a day, 50% saved, so 3 WP for each day. The price is locked, and only Gangsta can change it, in chat, when he hears a real reason. Time on the user's own block rules is sold by the quarter hour (15 minutes is a quarter of a day) for an app and its site together, and each buy on the same day costs double the one before. Any buy can be undone in its first 10 minutes. The price rule lives in one value in the backend; the PC and the phone only show the prices they are sent, so a different price system is one change in one place. A phone tap is applied on the satellite at once and folded on the PC under the same id, with the time of the tap, so a wait or an undo window is judged the same on both. A refused buy is answered with the reason and is not queued. The Crew board shows the other man the rewards only, never the buys or the blocked apps.

latestUpdates.item: Routines count per period of their repeat
latestUpdates.detail: A routine quest repeats on its own task's repeat (every day, week or month, every N days, or on chosen weekdays), and its target is the count for one period, such as three gym sessions a week. Each log counts toward the period that holds now; at the full count it can be claimed, and it pays once for that period. The next period starts again from 0. A missed period pays nothing, takes nothing, and keeps no streak. Weeks run Sunday to Saturday and a day starts at local midnight. Nothing is reset by a job: the note keeps the period its count was logged in and the period it was paid for, and a reader that finds an older one reads 0 and unpaid, so a period that passes with every device off is fresh the moment anything looks. Claiming ticks the task's instance, which rolls its schedule to the next one; a rule on chosen weekdays skips the other days. The PC add-quest form and the phone's quest forms ask how a routine repeats; counts read like 2/3 this week. The backend and the phone are checked against the same period cases; 550 phone unit tests pass.

latestUpdates.item: A quest's WP comes from its time and effort
latestUpdates.detail: Every new quest is priced by one formula: S = 1 + log2(1 + t/15) + 0.75C + 0.85R + 0.55E, and the WP is S rounded, at least 1, with no cap. t is the estimated active minutes for the whole quest; C, R and E are concentration (0 to 3), resistance to starting (0 to 4) and physical or emotional effort (0 to 3), rated against written definitions that the form shows word for word. Each extra stretch of time counts less than the one before. The quest type still changes the result: Milestone and Challenge add 1, Recovery pays half. The label (Tiny 1-3, Normal 4-6, Hard 7-9, Very Hard 10+) comes from the WP before the type changes it, and only describes. The add-quest form, the progress log, the suggestion editor and the approval cards on the PC, and the three quest forms on the phone, share one design: a time in HH:MM with a Total or Each switch for a quest done more than once, and one row of buttons per factor. A new quest starts with every level at 0 and cannot be added without a time. The phone sends the rating, never a WP number; the always-on process and the PC price it. Gangsta's own proposals rate the same factors. Quests made before keep their old price. The pick-a-difficulty box and the hand-typed WP on a progress log are gone. The Go backend, the PC form and the phone are checked against the same price cases; 546 phone unit tests pass.

latestUpdates.item: Quests are tasks on the phone too
latestUpdates.detail: The phone reads a quest off its task's note instead of matching the task's file name or title against the skill tree, which is how a quest whose task had been filed, renamed or copied lost its buttons. Home, the calendar and the task editor show a quest's own button (log, did it, or claim N WP) and Fail, never Done; a finished quest reads as paid or failed; a tap on its way shows at once without being counted twice when the notes arrive. Progress logs are left out of the task lists. The End Week button is gone. Editing a task's tags keeps its quest tag, and a parked task's parked tag, which a tag edit used to drop. A task with no title field reads its title off its file name, as the PC does. It uses only what the satellite already serves: the quest fields on task notes and the existing quest taps. 541 unit tests pass, and the build is installed on the phone.

latestUpdates.item: A quest has its own buttons on every PC screen
latestUpdates.detail: A quest is finished by claiming it, never by a tick. On the Tasks page a quest's menu offers its button (Log, Did it, or Claim N WP) and Fail quest, the detail card has the same two buttons and no Done status, and a finished quest reads as "✓ +N WP" or a grey "✗ Failed" in the Done list; undoing a fail is reopening its task. In the calendar a quest block's menu offers the same buttons instead of Mark done, and so does a planned quest in a day plan. The task editor shows a quest box with progress, WP and the two buttons, has no Done to set by hand, and now sends a status only when it changed (it used to re-stamp a done task as finished today on every save). The Command Post's main-task button becomes the quest's button when the main task is a quest. Underneath, every way of marking a task done ends in one function, and it now refuses a quest nobody has claimed or failed, so a chat tool or a missed screen cannot close one unpaid; reopening a claimed quest is refused too, because its WP is paid. The button rules live in one place, shared by every screen.

latestUpdates.item: Quests are tasks
latestUpdates.detail: A quest is now a task note that carries the quest's own fields (skill, type, difficulty, target, progress, reward, status), instead of a separate record in the skill tree held to a task by a link that kept drifting. The skill tree, the phone and the Crew board read the same quest list as before: it is filled from the task store on every read and never written to the tree file. The tree keeps the money - WP, badges, the ledger, and a list of quests already paid - so a claim pays once even when its second write, closing the task, is lost. On its first start the PC moves its quests onto their tasks; a satellite shows quests it has not seen moved as read-only until the PC pushes both files. Y's tree on the Crew board has its own task store for its quests. A quest made on the phone gets its ids at the satellite, derived from the tap's own id, so both machines make the same quest and a resent tap makes no second one; the route also stops dropping the phone form's type, tracking and unit. Quest taps on the satellite wait in the notes overlay, which the PC releases by recording the tap's id in its notes file. End Week is gone, so a one-time quest no longer goes back to zero at the end of a week. Failing a quest closes its task. A progress log is a task born done and is not listed on the Tasks page. New tasks keep their title as typed, where they used to read it back off a cleaned-up, numbered file name. Before the move, 74 leftover copies of five quests' tasks - made by an old bug that minted a new task on every page load - were deleted at the owner's request.

latestUpdates.item: Tasks page: a quest's task shows its quest controls
latestUpdates.detail: On the Tasks page a quest's task now shows the quest mark, its progress and its Log / Claim button, and can no longer be ticked done like a plain task. The page looked quests up by the task's path with its capitals, while the rows are keyed in lower case, so no quest ever matched: the controls were never drawn, and ticking such a task closed it without paying any WP. The key is now built the same way on both sides, with a test. The shop's seven placeholder rewards were also removed, at the owner's request.

latestUpdates.item: Crew board on a phone: one row on top, and pinch to zoom
latestUpdates.detail: In skill tree mode the board's top is one row again on a phone: the two names, then small icons for Board, Skill tree, Settings and Log out (the words come back on a wide screen). The 'read only' line under it is gone; Y's AI money for the month stays on the Settings page. The phone version of the tree now zooms with two fingers, around the point between them, as the phone app does.

latestUpdates.item: Crew board: the phone's skill tree on a phone
latestUpdates.detail: Opened on a phone, the Crew board's skill tree now looks like the phone app's Skill Tree tab instead of the desktop page squeezed small. A small 'PC view' / 'Phone view' switch picks the other one, and the choice is remembered on that device. Nothing about who may change what is different. In the phone app itself the branch list is gone: the tree tab always shows the whole tree, and the switch for abandoned branches moved under it.

latestUpdates.item: New: Commitments and rules
latestUpdates.detail: A Commitments page with two tabs. Commitments sit on a timeline by deadline with a Today mark; when a deadline comes the card asks 'Did you keep it?' with Kept, Broke, or Good reason (a break with a reason costs nothing and the reason is kept). Rules have their own fine per break and their exceptions written under them. Templates turn a repeat commitment into one click. Chat can read all of it but never change it. The phone has its own tab for all of it and works with the laptop off. The sidebar shows how many deadlines wait for an answer. The Activity page's old Rules tab is now called Block rules.

latestUpdates.item: Fixed: Gangsta no longer stays offline after the internet comes back
latestUpdates.detail: While offline, Gangsta checked for the way back by connecting to one public address only. On a network that blocks that one address it stayed offline until a restart, even with the internet working. It now tries a few addresses at once (two public ones, the AI service and the satellite) and is back online as soon as any one answers. The OFFLINE tag in the title bar is now a button: pressing it checks right away, shows Checking, and then either disappears or says still offline for a few seconds.

latestUpdates.item: Changed: the skill tree on the accountability board gets the whole window
latestUpdates.detail: In Skill tree mode everything above the tree fits in one thin row: the two tabs, the Board / Skill tree switch, the tree's own line (read only, the AI money) and the buttons. The tree's zoom and drag feel the same as in Gangsta for both men (speed 1.7x, acceleration 2.0x, 50 ms smoothing, momentum 1.7x).

latestUpdates.item: New: each man's skill tree on the accountability board, one tab per man
latestUpdates.detail: The board now shows one man per tab, on the computer as on the phone, with a Board / Skill tree switch. The skill tree is Gangsta's own skill tree page in a board mode. GBN's tree comes from Gangsta and is read only there. The other man gets the full skill tree on the board itself, kept apart on the satellite and copied to the PC as a backup, with the AI buttons inside a monthly limit that only GBN can change, and no coach chat. A new Settings page lets each man choose what the other sees: single skills, whole areas, and tabs of the skill window (notes, resources and the Manage tab start hidden). Hidden parts are removed on the satellite before anything is sent. The other man's tree starts empty: no starter areas or skills, only the generic shop rewards.

latestUpdates.item: Fixed: the climb looks right with only one step
latestUpdates.detail: The mountain in a skill's Path tab is now never shorter than its box, so a short path no longer leaves the bottom of the window empty; the steps keep their spacing from START and the slope above them is open rock up to the summit. A path with one step puts it in the middle, straight above START, and every path's trail now leaves from START instead of beginning in mid-air.

latestUpdates.item: Changed: one account on the accountability board was updated
latestUpdates.detail: One account's details on the accountability board were updated. The board's own test no longer needs any real account data in the code: it checks the same way with a throwaway test account.

latestUpdates.item: Fixed: six small prompt bugs the Prompt Feed review found
latestUpdates.detail: Saving a memory no longer calls the AI when no key is set. Memory roll-ups no longer cut a long day in the middle: the record stays valid JSON, drops its source links and its last events first (saying how many), and never splits a letter; the memory tagger's cut keeps whole letters too. Alarm lines are written for the day the batch is for, not always tomorrow. Quest from a task no longer offers hidden skills, and when the AI's skill pick is not one of the offered skills, the card asks you to choose instead of quietly picking the first one. Path next steps puts your resources under their own heading, so they no longer read as things you know. The video classifier now recognises a video site's own page names when they carry an unread count, so they are not classified as videos; the stored ones are cleared.

latestUpdates.item: Prompt Feed: every AI prompt is listed now, with its message and a decision graph
latestUpdates.detail: The Back-End page's Prompt Feed showed 11 prompts; the app sends about 30. It now lists all of them: the chat's fetching rounds and warden decision round, chat titles, the memory prompts, the skill and task prompts, recommendations, the video wall, the watch list, the alarm, the warden report, the games, the video classifier and the recipe painter. Each entry has three views: Flow (how the app decides to make the call, with yes/no arrows), Instructions and Message (what goes in the user's turn). The chat, coach, thought-chat and summary entries now show the full real prompt; before, parts were missing. Each prompt is built by the same function as the real call, and a test reads the source and fails when a model call has no entry. Also fixed: two out-of-date chat rules (tasks can be put on the calendar from chat; memory no longer lives in a notes folder), a dead memory prompt was removed, and the thought chat's opening line now runs on the medium model the routing table says. The Warden and Plan my day entries show their real message as well; the warden's leaves out the phone's blocks, because the page never goes online.

latestUpdates.item: Fixed: the touchpad pinch stays smooth after Alt+Tab, and the window trick is gone
latestUpdates.detail: After the main window stopped using the keep-running setting, the window-events log showed every pinch smooth, including right after an Alt+Tab, the case that always broke before and that the old trick never covered. The maximise-and-back nudge the app did at start and when the window came back is removed. The log stays on, so any jumpy pinch that ever returns will show what came before it.

latestUpdates.item: The real cause of the jumpy touchpad pinch: the main window's keep-running setting
latestUpdates.detail: The Electron upgrade did not fix it, so the cause was narrowed down with a bare test window: with Electron's backgroundThrottling turned off (the main window's setting, there so the pomodoro ends on time while hidden) the pinch broke after one Alt+Tab; with it left on, it stayed smooth; Chrome and Edge never had the problem. In Electron's code, that setting stops the page from ever counting as hidden, but Chromium still hides the page's inner window that receives the smooth pinch, and the step that shows it again only runs for a page that was hidden. The main window now uses the normal setting, and Chromium's disable-background-timer-throttling switch keeps the page timers on time instead: measured with a window minimised for 7 minutes, a page timer fired every 60 seconds without the switch and every second with it. The pomodoro and the time-limit pop-ups keep their timing with no code change, and a hidden window now stops drawing. The maximise nudge stays until the log shows the pinch smooth after an Alt+Tab.

latestUpdates.item: Desktop app moved from Electron 32 to Electron 45, for the touchpad pinch
latestUpdates.detail: The window-events log showed the third trigger for the jumpy pinch: switching windows. A quick Alt+Tab of 0.7 seconds was enough. Chromium treats a fully covered window like a hidden one and moves the page's inner window under a hidden parent, and Chromium 128 (inside Electron 32) threw the touchpad helper away and built a new one on every such move. From Chromium 140 a feature keeps the one helper and only re-points it, and it is on by default in Chromium 156, which Electron 45 ships. None of the Electron APIs the app uses were removed between 32 and 45 (checked against Electron's breaking-changes list), and all sixteen pages were opened on the packaged build with no console or page errors. The maximise nudge at start and on restore stays until the log shows the upgrade alone keeps the pinch smooth. Each pinch line in the log now also says where the pointer was.

latestUpdates.item: The touchpad fix itself was the wrong kind of nudge
latestUpdates.detail: The window-events log showed the one-pixel resize running right after a restore and the next pinch still coming in steps of 100; maximising the window then made every pinch smooth. So the nudge never worked for a normal-sized window. It now steps the window to maximised and straight back within one tick (a maximised window already did the reverse), at start and whenever the window comes back. If the step back lands anywhere other than where the window was, the log says so and the window is put back. Whether this fixes it is for the log to show on the next pinch.

latestUpdates.item: Fixed: the touchpad pinch was jumpy from the moment the app started
latestUpdates.detail: The new window-events log found the trigger on the first try: right after a launch, with nothing else happening, the very first pinch on the skill tree came in as whole steps of 100 instead of small smooth ones. The app already nudged the window size by one pixel when it came back from the taskbar or the tray, which brings the smooth pinch back, but a window shown at creation never fires that event, so a fresh start was never nudged. It now nudges once when the page has loaded. The log stays on, so it can show the fix holding and catch any other trigger.

latestUpdates.item: A window-events log to find why the touchpad pinch turns into jumps
latestUpdates.detail: Sometimes the touchpad pinch on the skill tree stops being smooth and zooms in big jumps until the window is resized, even though the app already nudges the window size when it comes back from the taskbar or the tray. The likely cause is Windows' smooth-gesture helper getting stuck and falling back to plain wheel steps, but nothing recorded what happened before, so the trigger is unknown. The desktop app now writes a small local log of window events (focus, hide and show, minimise and restore, resize, sleep and wake, lock and unlock, display changes, tab changes) and one line per pinch with its raw step sizes, marked smooth or stepped. It is a record only and changes nothing about the window; the log is size-capped, stays on the PC and holds no content from the app.

latestUpdates.item: Chat replies show what they actually did; phone chats get titles, traces and costs
latestUpdates.detail: Every assistant message now carries the tools it ran that change something, one line each taken from the tool's own result (reading tools are left out), and the chat on the PC and on the phone shows them under the reply with a tick, or a cross for a failure. A reply's words can still be wrong; the lines under it come from what ran. Chats answered by the satellite had three gaps, now closed: a thread started on the phone stayed 'New chat' for good because the fold that was meant to name it never did (the satellite now names it after the first reply, and the PC names any thread folded without one); 'What happened' on the PC found nothing because the trace stayed on the satellite's disk (the trace entry, without the prompt, now rides the exchange and is kept once); and the spend for those turns never reached the PC's cost ledger (its ledger row now rides along too, counted once). The existing rule against claiming an action that did not happen was tightened in place rather than added to: it now also forbids 'I'm doing it now' without the tool call in the same reply.

latestUpdates.item: Fixed: the skill tree could get stuck at one edge after a background reload
latestUpdates.detail: When data changed elsewhere, the tree page reloaded and briefly showed a loading screen, which threw the canvas away and built a new one. The size watcher still watched the removed canvas and read its size as zero, so the pan limits held the tree against one edge, the overview's view box shrank to a dot and zooming jumped against the same limit, until a tab switch or a resize measured again. A reload over a tree already on screen now updates it in place, a zero size is ignored, and a rebuilt canvas is watched and measured; a test fakes a background reload and checks the canvas and the overview box.

latestUpdates.item: The skill path is on the phone too
latestUpdates.detail: The phone's skill sheet now opens on a Path tab, which replaced Quests, laid out like the phone page of the open-book design: the climb on top (a mountain read from the bottom, steps more than one ahead in a cloud unless the fog is off, obstacles beside the step they block, a thin rail scroller with a dot per step, and a button back to the current step), then a line about the last change, the chosen step's page with what can be done there, the skill's quests with the step each belongs to, and what is known with its older versions. Every change is an ordinary tree action through the phone's outbox, with the phone's date and no ids; the satellite mints the ids, so a tap made twice is applied once. Finishing the last planned step also asks for next-step ideas once, queued behind the finish. The phone works out zones, fog and the 'what just happened' line with a copy of the desk's rules, tested on the same cases. The sheet now fills the screen with coloured index tabs; Manage has the fog switch; Progress grades the same three numbers as the desk; History adds the steps walked and the changes to what is known, by month. One difference: adding a quest as its own new step works only on the desk, because the phone learns a new step's id only after the satellite answers.

latestUpdates.item: The PC skill window's other tabs now match the open book
latestUpdates.detail: Progress shows the badge ladder with a bar toward the next badge; a "How I'm doing" row of three numbers that have a clear good or bad (days in a row with progress, active days this week, days since the last progress), each coloured good, okay or low and always with a sign and a word; plain counts in gold (WP earned, WP this week, steps walked, quests claimed, things known); the weekly WP chart redrawn with a round-number axis, a value only on this week and the best week, and a value on hover; and the progress log as striped rows. Activities explains that the list is what counts as progress and pays nothing by itself. Notes has two sub-tabs, the own note and Gangsta's, as ruled boxes of the same size that both stay loaded, plus a button that opens the skill's coach chat in the Chat tab. History is a month-by-month timeline that now also lists the path steps walked, obstacles cleared and changes to what is known. Manage is laid out as sections with chips, segmented choices, the three medals with their real thresholds, switches for lock, hide and fog, and dark menus. The grading rules are small tested functions, and each tab has a test that was checked by breaking the rule it guards.

latestUpdates.item: Fixed: the skill window's Notes tab could show an empty box over a saved note
latestUpdates.detail: The notes were written into their boxes only when a skill was opened, but the window opens on another tab, so the Notes boxes did not exist yet and stayed empty. The next keystroke then saved that empty box over the real note. The loaded text is now kept and written into a box whenever the box appears; a test pins it.

latestUpdates.item: The companion has a second color for pomodoro focus blocks, and the Classic face takes colors too
latestUpdates.detail: Settings → Companion now has two colors, a normal one and one for pomodoro (Cyan, Green, Amber or Magenta; the pomodoro one starts as Amber), with a preview of each. The companion wears the pomodoro color only while a focus block is actually running; breaks and a paused timer use the normal color. The timer runs in the main window, so it sets a flag in local storage and the floating companion window hears it the same way it hears the other avatar settings; the flag is cleared when the main window starts, so a crash mid-block cannot leave it on. The Retro face glows in the color; the Classic face, which had no color before, now has its eyes, eyebrows and edge tinted with it, while the strong state colors (angry red, celebrating gold, sleepy grey) still win. The rule for when the pomodoro color applies is a small tested function.

latestUpdates.item: The phone has the same skill window, and links can be shared into a skill from any app
latestUpdates.detail: The phone skill screen gained the why line, the Next step card, a Resources tab (the same learning queue, with add, start, done, pin and delete; files show as kept on the PC), the practice boards by name, a History tab and the weekly WP chart, read from a new history route. Sharing a link from another app offers Gangsta; it asks which skill and adds the link to that skill's queue through the satellite, which looks up the title once so both machines store the same row.

latestUpdates.item: A skill window redesigned around what to do next, with resources attached to each skill
latestUpdates.detail: The skill window keeps its old footprint but splits into two columns. The left one holds the name, a one-line "why I am learning this", the badge bar and a Next step card (the active quest, else a pinned or started resource, else the assistant's first quest idea, else the next resource waiting), and it folds to a thin strip. The right one has seven tabs: Quests, Progress (badge ladder and a twelve-week WP chart), Resources, Activities, Notes, History and Manage. Resources are links, online videos, files and short notes kept as a learning queue (to learn, learning, done, one pin). They live inside the skill record, so the phone can add and tick them through the existing tree action road with an id minted by the satellite; file bytes are copied into a folder that is not synced. Videos play in the built-in player and remember where they stopped. History and the chart are read from the existing WP ledger plus the resource dates; badges are found where the running total crossed a threshold. A Find resources button makes one paid model call with web search and only keeps addresses the search returned. The coach and the quest drafter now see the why line and the resource titles. Practice boards linked to a skill show in its window; a small summary of them is written into the synced skill-tree folder so the phone can list them.

latestUpdates.item: The PC calendar adds by right-click or one Add button, and time blocks no longer hide each other
latestUpdates.detail: Right-clicking an empty spot of the day or week grid opens a menu at that 15-minute slot: a task (the small form, now a pop-up so the week can use it), a time block (a saved block or bundle placed at that time, or a one-off block for that day only) or an activity (searchable list, placed for its usual length, or a new one through the full form). One Add button replaces the two old add buttons; it starts at the next free slot, and saved blocks from it keep their usual time. Two new backend calls place a template or a bundle at a chosen start; a bundle keeps its inner spacing and drops a part pushed past midnight. Time blocks that share time are now drawn side by side on the PC (day and week) and on the phone, using the same lane packing as tasks; nothing is refused, because two things really can be booked at once. Also fixed: on the Plan, pressing Add on an activity also opened its editor, because the press reached the row behind the button.

latestUpdates.item: Changes made on the phone show at once on every phone screen, and PC changes reach the phone within half a minute
latestUpdates.detail: A change made in the phone app only appeared on other screens when they were opened, or when the app came back to the front, and some not even then. Fixed in layers. (1) One signal: every write on the phone now says what kind of thing it changed (tasks and notes, cart, activities, blocks, the skill tree), and the main screen redraws what shows it. Notes edits say so the moment they are queued, before any network, and the screens draw the local copy plus the queue, so a task added from Home's '+' appears on Home at once even with no signal; Home and the calendar now read on a thread of their own instead of waiting behind the send. (2) Queues sent at once: an activity made on the Plan was queued and never sent until the app was reopened, which is why it only appeared after a restart; it is sent now, and the Plan asks the always-on process again, which applies phone changes on arrival. Block moves and workout sets queued in a dead spot are sent when the app comes back, not only from their own tabs; the calendar no longer replaces a queued move with the server's older copy. (3) Real bugs found on the way: the Plan's task editor saved on the main thread, which Android ends the app for, so saving or parking a task there most likely closed the app; notes writes are now locked so they stay in order from any thread. A background pull read today's blocks from the wrong place in the answer and saved an empty list over them every half hour. Tasks placed or moved on the Plan now pull the notes, so their new time shows on Home and the calendar. (4) While the app is open it checks every 30 seconds: notes by revision (a few bytes when nothing changed, and no redraw), and the cart or activity list when on screen, redrawing only if the revision moved. (5) On the PC, every 20-second heartbeat now pushes the synced files that changed since the last look, found by size and time alone; the full hash comparison stays every five minutes as the safety net and the only road for deletes, and append-only logs stay on it. (6) The open PC page reloads when a phone change is folded in: the backend keeps a revision number, the app reads it every 4 seconds, and each page reloads, except mid-drag or mid-edit. Tests: phone 6 new files (signal, alarm, rotation, chat, blocks pull, plan clock), Go 4, UI 2; sabotage rounds of 13, 8 and 3, all caught except one guard whose arithmetic already covers it.

latestUpdates.item: The planner starts from now, an alarm with no days rings once, turning the phone keeps the screen, and a new chat's first message shows once
latestUpdates.detail: Planner: on today's plan, time that has passed is no longer offered as room. At 16:00, adding to the late afternoon (15:00-18:00) used to place the thing at 15:00; the past is now cut off every free stretch, rounded up to the next five minutes, on the phone and the PC alike (the two use the same rule and the same test cases). Alarm: an alarm with no days already switched itself off after ringing, but two such alarms set to the same minute fire as one, and only the armed one was switched off, so the other rang again the next day; every ring-once alarm at the fired minute is now off, and the behaviour is tested through the real receiver. Rotation: turning the phone rebuilt the whole screen and only the tab number survived, so an open workout fell back to the list; the app now keeps its screens through a turn (one manifest attribute, guarded by a test), and the chat bubbles, the one thing sized from the screen width, re-measure. Chat: a new conversation drew its first message twice. The server had it once; a new thread's first poll is a full reload, which cleared the screen and then put the still-pending bubble back under its own echo, because the bubble had been matched against the screen it had just been cleared from. It is matched against the pending list now.

latestUpdates.item: The recipe book can paint a picture of a recipe
latestUpdates.detail: Most recipes came over from an older app without a photo. An open recipe now has 'Paint a picture': its name, ingredients and method go to OpenAI's image model (gpt-image-2.5-flare, medium quality) after a house style the owner wrote, a 1930s-50s American food advertisement, which can be changed in Settings -> Recipes and reset to the default. The result is a draft and nothing changes until Keep: it shows beside the current picture with what it cost, with Keep, Try again and Cancel. Drafts live in a folder outside recipes/, which syncs, so a turned-down picture never reaches the satellite or the phone; Try again and leaving the page throw drafts away, and anything left over is swept after a day. The model cannot be asked for 1200x900 (edges must be multiples of 16), so it is asked for 1280x960, which is exactly 4:3, and scaled to 1200x900 by an area-averaging resampler, since the standard library has none; nothing is cut off. Each call is recorded in the AI cost ledger from the usage counts OpenAI returns, at the published rates. Tests: Go 8 (prompt, crop, scaling, the 1200x900 JPEG, path escapes, the style setting, keep and discard, the price), 7 of 8 sabotages caught, the eighth removing a guard the read side already covers; UI 2, both sabotages caught. Checked in the packaged app: the button and the Settings tab render, and the drafts route refuses a path escape. No real picture has been painted in testing, since every one costs money.

latestUpdates.item: Touchpad zoom stays smooth after the window comes back from the taskbar
latestUpdates.detail: After the window was minimised and brought back in its normal (not maximised) size, a touchpad pinch on the skill tree zoomed in fixed jumps of about a fifth instead of smoothly. Maximising cured it until the next minimise. This is not the skill tree: Chromium receives a precision touchpad's gestures through Windows' Direct Manipulation, and after a minimise the window loses that hookup, so Windows falls back to plain wheel steps. Any resize restores it, which is why maximising helped. The main window now changes its width by one pixel and back whenever it is restored from the taskbar or shown from the tray. A maximised window ignores a size change, and the owner found it loses the touchpad too, so a maximised one leaves and re-enters the maximised state in the same instant instead; that resizes the page without a visible frame (a red test window, its corner sampled every 7 ms through the restore, never showed anything else), and the size it returns to on restore-down is kept. Checked in the packaged app through Windows itself: normal 900x600, 901x600 for a moment, 900x600 again; maximised before and after, and restore-down still 900x600. Whether the pinch is smooth again can only be felt on the real touchpad; synthetic input does not go through Direct Manipulation.

latestUpdates.item: The skill tree moves under a two-finger touchpad slide, also while pinching
latestUpdates.detail: Every wheel event on the skill tree zoomed, so on a laptop touchpad there was no way to move the view without letting go and dragging, and none at all during a pinch. The browser delivers a pinch as a wheel event with the control key set, and a two-finger slide as a plain wheel event with small, often diagonal amounts. Those are now told apart: a pinch zooms, a slide moves by exactly its amounts, and a mouse wheel notch (a large, purely vertical amount) still zooms. A fast slide can look like a notch, so once a gesture is known to come from a touchpad it stays one for half a second. A slide during a zoom moves both the target and the frame on screen, so the two combine instead of fighting. The decision is a small pure function with its own tests, each checked by breaking it; checked in the running app with real input events: slide moved without zooming, pinch plus slide did both, a notch zoomed.

latestUpdates.item: A new kind of block rule: a time limit counted across the PC and the phone together
latestUpdates.detail: The other rules block on a clock or until something is done. This one blocks on time spent: a list of apps and sites is COUNTED, and when their combined time reaches a limit, a second list is BLOCKED until the counter resets. The two lists are separate on purpose, and the form recommends blocking what is counted. The reset is configurable: every N hours, days or weeks, at a chosen time, on a chosen weekday; midnight every day by default. The rule can be limited to some days of the week, and it warns at chosen minutes before the limit (10 and 1 by default; can be turned off). Each device counts its own time from what it already records: the PC from its activity store, including the stretch still open; the phone from the system usage log and its own record of site visits. Each reports to the always-on process, which keeps the combined total in a file of its own that is never synced, and is the source of truth for it. Each device enforces with its own live count plus the other side's last known count, so a lost connection can delay a block but never cancel one. The rule rides the existing condition machinery: its condition is time-limit plus the rule's id, and 'met' means still under the limit, the same direction as every other condition. That is what let the browser extension, the hub's verdict stamp and an older phone build carry it unchanged. The counting window is computed separately on the PC, the always-on process and the phone, so the two implementations are held to the same test cases, including a clock change. Tests: Go 18 plus a sabotage round of ten (one gap found and closed: a rule switched off for the day still showed as reached); the app 18 plus a sabotage round of eight; the form 7.

latestUpdates.item: The skill tree is drawn as cards; the shopping cart and the stored-facts page are reachable again
latestUpdates.detail: The skill tree was one row of branch panels under a root node, so with sixteen branches it was thousands of pixels wide and only fitted at a size where nothing could be read. Each branch is now a card holding its own focus tree, and the cards wrap into rows. The canvas, zoom and overview map stay, at the owner's request. A tile is an icon over a name, with the badge hanging under it as a ribbon; a skill with no progress keeps a gray icon, so the few that are moving stand out. The dashed lines that joined related skills across branches are gone, because between cards they crossed the whole canvas; pressing a skill now makes its related skills glow instead. The layout is pure and has its own tests: cards never overlap, every tile stays inside its card, a card wider than the wrap width gets a row of its own. Each was checked by breaking it on purpose. Separately: the shopping cart had a tab under Tasks until the task list was rebuilt, when the new header was drawn without the switch. The cart and its data were intact and nothing led to them. The switch is back, it remembers the last tab, and the task keys only act on the task tab, so a letter typed on the cart cannot finish a task nobody can see. And the page listing what the assistant has stored about the owner moved from the sidebar into the back-end page as its last tab; old links to it land there.

latestUpdates.item: Activities can be edited from the day planner, like tasks
latestUpdates.detail: In the day planner, pressing a task opened its editor and pressing an activity beside it did nothing: the activity editor lived only on the screen that lists activities. It now opens from the planner too, on a press and from an 'Edit' line at the top of the right-click menu. It is not a second editor. The one that existed was moved into a component of its own, and both screens now open that same one, so the two cannot drift apart when a new kind of column is added. It carries everything the original did: name, icon, type, usual length, a note, his own columns, and delete, which still needs a second press. Editing changes the activity, not the blocks already placed on the calendar from it; those keep their own name and length, by his choice. Driving the real planner caught what the component tests could not: the activity rows had never had a press handler at all, so the editor was wired and unreachable. Five sabotages on the editor, all caught.

latestUpdates.item: Right-click menus ran off the bottom of the window
latestUpdates.detail: A right-click near the bottom of the Plan showed a menu's title and first row; the rest was below the window. The Plan, and the Skill Tree, each drew their own menu at the mouse and never asked whether it fit. The shared menu every other page uses did ask, but only half the question: a menu taller than the window was pushed to the top and still ran off the bottom. There is now one placement rule and every menu in the app uses it: below the cursor if it fits, otherwise above it, the way a desktop opens a menu near the bottom edge; right of the cursor if it fits, otherwise left of it; and never larger than the window, past which it scrolls inside itself. The Plan and the Skill Tree now use the shared menu and keep their own look. The companion's menus are the operating system's own and were already safe. Measured on the real Plan: right-clicking the bottom row in a 600-pixel window opened the menu upward with all seven rows visible.

latestUpdates.item: Long videos from the big video site stopped after one minute
latestUpdates.detail: Videos from the large video site played for about a minute and froze for good. Measured in the running player: it sat at 59.8 seconds while the next piece of audio was refused four times. The site had begun serving the client the app identifies as only the first minute or so, and refusing every byte after it unless the request carries a 'proof of origin' stamp issued by the site's own bot-check script. Producing that stamp is passing the site's bot detection on purpose, and this app does not do that. Other open projects were compared first: the ones that produce the stamp, public relay servers (most of them gone, and each one sees what you watch), bundling a separate downloader, and the site's official player (refused here: it shows adverts). Then the clients the site serves WITHOUT the stamp were measured on real videos, asking for bytes at the start, past one minute, at eighty percent and at the end. One of them served every byte, at 1080p, on five videos up to an hour long, without running any of the site's code. That is now the client. It is the same kind of choice as before, and the site may close it too; a small script now reruns the whole measurement in seconds, so the next time videos stop at a minute the answer is one command away. Downloads were broken the same way and nobody had noticed, because they had only ever been tested on the other source. They work again, and are now fetched in ten-megabyte pieces the way the player asks: a two-and-a-half-minute video went from 163 seconds to 12, byte for byte identical. Videos that need a signed-in adult account still cannot play; no signed-out method that works today was found, and that is left for later on purpose.

latestUpdates.item: Classifying a site from the day's log: two menus, no change, and half the rows left behind
latestUpdates.detail: One click on a site's category opened two menus, and choosing a category appeared to do nothing. Three separate faults produced that one experience. The menu was identified by the rule it would save, so every row of the same site opened its own copy at once -- each dropping under its own row, so they looked as though they belonged to other entries. A menu now belongs to the row it was opened on. The choice did save; the row went on showing 'unknown' because of a fix made earlier the same day, which re-reads rules for rows that HAD a rule when recorded and skipped rows that had none -- which are, by definition, the ones anyone classifies. Those rows now follow a rule made later, looked up by where they came from, so a website with no rule never borrows the browser's own app rule. And a rule on one address of a shop did not reach its other address: the Hebrew storefront and the payment pages were different subdomains. Choosing a category from the log now classifies the whole site, folding together only versions of one site -- www, mobile, a two-letter language code -- never different services on one domain, and never down to a bare country suffix. Older rules on another version of the same site are removed, since a more specific rule would otherwise go on overriding the new one. Measured on the real day afterwards: one menu per click, and every row of the site changed. Seven sabotages, all caught.

latestUpdates.item: A new video player, and two marks every video remembers
